site_model.what_it_is: A service that creates personalised, illustrated digital storybooks featuring family members and can also produce printed hardcover books.
site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting to preserve a child and a favourite grown-up, sibling, or pet in a story based on a real memory.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a family memory and treasured details into an illustrated storybook, with a free digital preview and printed hardcovers shipped across the UK.
main_tasks: Log in to an existing account
Provide a place, treasured object, and memory
Generate and read an illustrated storybook
Check pricing for a printed hardcover
site_model.pricing_model: The digital preview is advertised as free, while printed hardcovers are available for a fee. No actual price is shown here.
trust_signals: A three-step explanation of the process
Claims that preview generation takes about a minute
site_model.fit_for_me: Very relevant because I can create a story starring my five-year-old daughter, Sam, and her Grandpa Joe, based on a beach memory and her yellow bucket.

127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories, bound for generations.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.title: StoryHearth – Personalised storybooks starring your family
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.observation: The StoryHearth homepage explains that families can turn characters and a shared memory into an illustrated digital storybook, with printed hardcovers available in the UK. I can see prominent links to log in, view pricing, learn how it works, or proceed to creation.
127.0.0.1:8765/ | Your family's stories,.think_aloud: This looks relevant to me. The wording “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “lived-experience corpus” sounds far too technical for a normal family, but the three-step explanation underneath is clear enough. I came here to use my account, so I’ll choose “Log in” rather than “Proceed.”

review.purpose: Introduce the personalised storybook service, explain how it works, and offer paths to pricing, login, and story creation.
review.what_is_happening: The homepage displays a hero message, two calls to action, a family-themed illustration, a three-step process, testimonials, FAQ controls, and footer links. No generated content is present.
review.first_impression: The warm cream design and simple three-step explanation make the service look friendly and relevant, but the opening paragraph is needlessly technical and the main illustration has no useful description.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I want to log in to my account and make our story.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the dark “Log in” button at the top right is prominent, and I can also see the “Proceed →” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Log in” exactly matches my immediate goal, while “Proceed” is less clear about whether it logs in or starts a new story.

issues.title: The main description uses unnecessarily technical language
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It makes the service sound cold and difficult, and I have to work out what it means.
issues.fix: Replace it with plain language, for example: “Turn a special family memory into a personalised storybook featuring your child and someone you love.”

issues.title: The prominent hero image lacks a useful description
issues.evidence: The image is shown with “no description” despite conveying the core family-book idea visually.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Someone using a screen reader or someone who cannot see the image would miss part of what the service offers.
issues.fix: Add concise alternative text that conveys the purpose, such as “An open personalised storybook featuring two family members.”

issues.title: The image is marked as decorative-looking but carries meaning
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The illustration is one of the strongest visual signals that this is about family stories, but it feels generic and detached from the text.
issues.fix: Use a more relevant image showing a child and grandparent with a storybook, or pair the existing graphic with a clear caption.

positives: The three simple headings “Tell us who,” “Share a memory,” and “We write & illustrate” make the process easy to understand.
“Log in” is visible without scrolling.
The page says the digital preview is free and mentions UK hardcover shipping.
The warm colours and typography create a family-friendly tone.

127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.title: Log in – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.observation: The StoryHearth login page shows a welcome-back card with email and password fields, a Log in button, and links for account creation, privacy, terms, and contact. The page is currently waiting for me to enter my account details.
127.0.0.1:8765/login.html | Welcome back.think_aloud: This looks straightforward. I can see the Email and Password boxes, so I will use my account details and click Log in. The lack of visible field labels is a small accessibility concern, but the placeholders make the purpose clear enough for me.

review.purpose: To sign into an existing StoryHearth account.
review.what_is_happening: The login form is empty and ready for an email address and password. A prominent Log in button is provided, along with a Create an account link and footer links.
review.first_impression: Simple and familiar. I know exactly what to do, although the input boxes are identified only by placeholder text rather than proper visible labels.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter my account details and try to sign in now.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the Email and Password fields and the Log in button are prominent.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. The placeholders “Email” and “Password” match what I want, but proper labels would be clearer and more reliable.

issues.title: Login fields lack programmatic visible labels
issues.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email" and [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can guess what the boxes are for, but placeholders are less accessible and may disappear while typing.
issues.fix: Add persistent visible labels such as “Email address” and “Password”, associated with each textbox, while keeping placeholders only as supplementary hints.

positives: The main login form is centered and easy to find.
The Log in button is prominent and clearly matches the next action.
The page provides a clear route to Create an account for new users.

127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.title: My books – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.observation: I have logged in and reached the “My books” dashboard. It says “You have no books yet” and offers a “+ Create a new book” button, but an error banner at the top says “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
127.0.0.1:8765/dashboard.html | Welcome.think_aloud: I can see where I need to go, but that error message is alarming and technical. I’m not sure whether it means my family details have not loaded properly, although I can still try creating a book.

review.purpose: Shows the books in my account and provides a way to create another one.
review.what_is_happening: The dashboard welcomes me, reports that I have no books, and displays a create button. However, it also shows a profile-sync error and a Log out link that appears to point back to the dashboard.
review.first_impression: The main task is obvious, but the ugly error code makes the page feel unreliable.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try creating a book because that is the next required step.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the orange “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes, “Create a new book” clearly matches what I want to do.

issues.title: Technical sync error creates doubt about account data
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am about to enter a family memory, and I cannot tell whether the sync problem means those details may be missing or lost.
issues.fix: Replace the code with a plain-language message such as “Some account details could not be loaded.” Explain what is affected and provide a Retry or Continue button if safe.

issues.title: Sync problem has no recovery guidance
issues.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.” There is no Retry, Help, or explanation beside the message.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I do not know whether I should keep going, refresh, or ask for help.
issues.fix: Add a short explanation and clear actions such as “Try again” and “Continue without syncing,” or a Contact support link.

issues.title: Log out link appears to point to the dashboard
issues.evidence: [5] link “Log out” -> /dashboard.html
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A logout control that does not log me out undermines my expectation of what the link will do.
issues.fix: Make the Log out link navigate to a genuine logged-out page or sign-in screen.

issues.title: Footer links have very low contrast
issues.evidence: The footer text “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” is extremely faint.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I can barely see or read these links, especially the legal and contact information.
issues.fix: Use a darker text colour with sufficient WCAG contrast and provide visible keyboard focus states.

positives: The “Welcome back, Demo” heading confirms that the site recognised the account.
The dashboard clearly says there are no books yet.
The “+ Create a new book” button is prominent and clearly labelled.
review.abandon_reason: The profile-sync warning worries me, but the main creation control is obvious enough to try.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.page_key: 127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the star of the story?
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.observation: The Create your book form asks who the main child is, their age, pronouns, appearance, and who else will appear in the story. It has a Next button, with relationship already set to Grandparent.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Who's the s.think_aloud: This is straightforward enough. I will enter Sam, choose age 5 and she/her, add brown hair, and include Grandpa Joe. The form does not yet ask what the family memory is, so I expect that on the next screen.

review.purpose: Collect the main child and another person for the personalised story.
review.what_is_happening: The form is ready for the child’s first name, age, pronouns, optional appearance, another character, and relationship. The relationship menu is already set to Grandparent.
review.first_impression: The form looks clear and neatly arranged. I can understand the fields quickly, although the earlier family-sync error makes me slightly wary that my details may not be fully working.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, this is exactly the setup I need before creating the story.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the labelled textboxes and dropdowns are easy to notice, and the orange Next button stands out.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Child’s first name”, “Age”, “Pronouns”, and “Who else is in the story?” match what I want to enter.

issues.title: No explanation of what happens next
issues.evidence: The screen ends with the button [12] “Next” and no visible hint that the next screen will ask for the memory itself.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know I need to add the beach memory eventually, but I am not sure whether I am missing a field on this screen.
issues.fix: Add a short line such as “Next, tell us the family memory you want to remember.”

positives: The form has a clear question: “Who’s the star of the story?”
The fields are grouped logically and the labels are visible.
The orange Next button is visually prominent.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.observation: This is the story-details step of the book creator. It asks for the location, a special object, and the family memory or idea, with Back and Next controls.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Your story.think_aloud: This is clear and easy to follow. I’ll say it was at the beach, include the yellow bucket, and describe building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe so the story is about our family memory.

review.purpose: Collect the setting, an important object, and the family memory to use when generating the personalised storybook.
review.what_is_happening: The user is on the second stage of creating a book. Three empty fields are presented for the story location, a special object, and the memory or idea behind the story.
review.first_impression: The page is calm, neatly laid out, and straightforward. The examples in the boxes make it obvious what to enter.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would fill in all three boxes because they match the memory I want in the book.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the three labelled text areas and the orange “Next” button are easy to notice.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Where does the story happen?”, “A special object”, and “Tell us the memory or idea behind your story” clearly match what I want to provide.

issues.title: Special object field is not marked optional
issues.evidence: “A special object” is presented as a field, while the preceding form used “(optional)” to identify optional information.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It is unclear whether I must include an object, although I happen to have a meaningful one.
issues.fix: Label this field “A special object (optional)” if it is not required, and similarly clarify whether the location and memory fields are required.

positives: The field labels plainly describe the information needed.
Helpful placeholders use familiar family-memory examples.
The form is uncluttered and the primary “Next” action stands out.
A clearly visible “Back” control preserves my ability to change earlier details.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.observation: The page is a “Choose the look & feel” step for setting the book's reading level and illustration style. “Lexile 200L–500L” and “Watercolour — soft and dreamy” are selected, with Back and Next buttons below.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Choose the.think_aloud: The reading level choices sound technical, but I can see that the middle range is already selected and that should suit Sam at age five. I’ll keep the soft watercolour look and click Next.

review.purpose: Choose how difficult the story should be and what the illustrations should look like.
review.what_is_happening: The form presents four Lexile reading-level ranges and three illustration styles. A middle reading range and the watercolour style are selected, and the user can continue with Next.
review.first_impression: It looks neat and easy, though “Lexile” is jargon I would not normally understand without more explanation.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would accept the sensible middle reading range already selected for a five-year-old and continue.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the selected radio button and the Next button are both clearly visible.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The illustration labels clearly describe the style, but the Lexile labels do not plainly tell me which range is intended for a five-year-old.

issues.title: Reading-level choices use unexplained jargon
issues.evidence: "Lexile BR–200L", "Lexile 200L–500L", "Lexile 500L–800L", and "Lexile 800L+"
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I know Sam is five, but the labels do not directly connect those number ranges to an age or reading ability.
issues.fix: Show an age-friendly label beside each range, such as “Lexile 200L–500L — approximately ages 5–8”, and include a short explanation of Lexile.

positives: The page clearly shows which reading level and illustration style are selected.
The watercolour option is described in plain, appealing language.
Back and Next controls are visible and easy to identify.

127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.title: Create your book – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.observation: The final creation step offers an optional photo upload so the illustrations can resemble the child. No photo is required, and there are Back and Create my book buttons.
127.0.0.1:8765/create.html | Add a photo.think_aloud: This is a clear final step. I do not have a photo available here, so I will leave it empty and click “Create my book” because the wording clearly says the upload is optional.

review.purpose: Collect an optional child photo that may be used to personalise the illustrations, then let the user create the book.
review.what_is_happening: The screen asks me to optionally upload a clear photo of the child's face. An empty file-upload control, a Back button, and a Create my book button are visible.
review.first_impression: This is straightforward and I understand that I can skip the photo. The page is clean, although I notice the upload control itself has no proper visible label.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would continue by creating the book without adding a photo.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I notice the prominent “Create my book” button and understand that “Add a photo (optional)” can be skipped.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Yes. “Create my book” clearly matches my goal, and the photo heading clearly says it is optional.

issues.title: File upload lacks a proper label
issues.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label); the control only displays “Choose file”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Someone using a screen reader may not know that this control is for a child's face photo, even though nearby instructions explain it.
issues.fix: Give the file input a persistent visible label such as “Child’s photo” and associate the explanatory text with it through accessible markup.

issues.title: Privacy reassurance is missing beside a child-photo upload
issues.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I would want to know how a child's photo is handled, retained, and shared before choosing to upload one.
issues.fix: Add a short note linking to the Privacy Policy and explaining whether the uploaded photo is used only for generation, stored, or deleted.

positives: The heading clearly says “(optional),” so skipping the upload feels acceptable.
The primary action has a specific, understandable label: “Create my book.”
A Back control is available before committing to creation.
The page is uncluttered and the main action is visually prominent.

127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.title: Your storybook – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.observation: The generated book preview has opened at page 1 of 9, titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” with a simple cover illustration. The page also shows regeneration and hardcover-order options below the fold, but the actual cover says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” despite Watercolour having been selected earlier.
127.0.0.1:8765/book.html | The Magical A.think_aloud: The book appeared, so the last action did work, but I’m disappointed by two obvious mistakes: “Adventrue” is misspelled, and this is a Pop-art comic when I chose Watercolour. I need to read all nine pages carefully before deciding whether these are isolated mistakes or make the whole book unsuitable.

review.purpose: Preview the newly generated family storybook page by page, then regenerate it or proceed to hardcover ordering.
review.what_is_happening: The first of nine generated pages is displayed with previous and next controls. A cover titled “The Magical Adventrue of Sam” is labelled as Pop-art comic, while controls farther down offer a $4.99 regeneration and an “Order hardcover” link.
review.first_impression: It is easy to see that a book was created, but the misspelling “Adventrue” makes it feel careless. I also immediately noticed that the cover says “Pop-art comic” even though I selected “Watercolour,” which makes me question whether my choices were applied.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try reading through the whole book because I need to check whether the beach memory, yellow bucket, Sam, and Grandpa Joe were included and whether the reading level is suitable for a five-year-old.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, the next-page control labelled “›” is obvious, and “1 / 9” makes it clear that there are eight more pages to inspect.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Partly. The arrow control works for turning pages, but the book metadata is unclear: “A StoryHearth original” does not explain that this is my generated story, and the style shown conflicts with my Watercolour choice.

issues.title: Selected illustration style was not applied
issues.evidence: The page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic,” even though Watercolour was the selected look on the previous screen.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I deliberately chose a soft Watercolour look, so the generated result is not what I asked for. It makes me distrust the other story settings too.
issues.fix: Apply the chosen Watercolour style and show the selected style in the generation summary so a mismatch is obvious and can be corrected.

issues.title: The generated title is misspelled
issues.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Sam”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: That spelling error appears prominently on the cover, so I would not want to print or pay for this book looking like this.
issues.fix: Add a title spell-check and let me edit the title before ordering.

issues.title: The preview does not visibly confirm personalisation
issues.evidence: The visible cover only shows the title and “Sam”; Grandpa Joe, the beach, the sandcastles, and the yellow bucket are not mentioned on this page.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know the site used all the family details I supplied, not just the child's first name.
issues.fix: After generation, show a short confirmation such as “Created using Sam, Grandpa Joe, the beach, the yellow bucket, and your memory,” or include this in an accessible summary.

issues.title: Generated preview regeneration has an immediate charge
issues.evidence: [8] “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I may want to fix the wrong style, but I would want to know exactly what this charges for and whether it affects the whole book before clicking it.
issues.fix: Explain the regeneration price in a confirmation dialog and state that it replaces the whole book, without pre-selecting or enabling payment automatically.

positives: The successful generation is shown clearly through a nine-page preview.
Page position is shown as “1 / 9,” so I know there are more pages.
The next-page arrow is prominent and easy to find.
There is a clear path to “Order hardcover” for checking the final price later.

later_issues.title: The final page does not fit the family memory well
later_issues.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Sam looked up at the sky, she would always remember”
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Our memory was a day at the beach building sandcastles with Grandpa Joe, so looking at the sky feels disconnected from what we asked for.
later_issues.fix: Generate an ending that refers clearly to the beach, sandcastles, Grandpa Joe, and the yellow bucket.

later_issues.title: “The End” is repeated twice on the last page
later_issues.evidence: The image says “The End,” and the sentence below also ends with “The End”
later_issues.why_it_matters_to_me: It looks redundant and a bit unfinished.
later_issues.fix: Show the final wording only once, or use separate roles for the image text and printed page text.

127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.title: Checkout – StoryHearth
127.0.0.1:8765/checkout.html | Checkout.observation: The checkout shows a £24.99 hardcover, £7.99 premium gift wrap, £12.99 shipping & handling, and a £45.97 total. Premium gift wrap is already checked without me asking, and the page also requests an address and payment details before an offscreen “Pay now” button.

review.purpose: Shows the cost of ordering the generated hardcover and collects delivery and payment information.
review.what_is_happening: The checkout displays the hardcover for “The Magical Adventrue of Sam,” with a countdown, item prices, shipping, total, and empty address and payment fields. Premium gift wrap is pre-selected.
review.first_impression: The prices are visible, but I am annoyed that premium gift wrap is already selected. The checkout makes the order feel much more expensive than the £24.99 book price alone.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would try to inspect the full cost, but I would not proceed with payment.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the “Premium gift wrap” checkbox and the itemised prices.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The labels clearly identify the hardcover, gift wrap, shipping, total, address, and payment fields, so they mostly match what I want to check.

issues.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
issues.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), with £7.99 shown beside it
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I did not choose gift wrap, so the site is adding £7.99 without my permission and making the total higher.
issues.fix: Leave optional extras unchecked by default and show the additional cost immediately beside the checkbox.

issues.title: Checkout is not showing what the basic delivered hardcover costs before extras
issues.evidence: The page shows “Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Sam £24.99,” “Shipping & handling £12.99,” and a separate checked “Premium gift wrap £7.99.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The individual prices are there, but the headline total is £45.97, and it is not immediately obvious that the book plus delivery would be £37.98 without gift wrap.
issues.fix: Show a clear subtotal for the book and delivery, and update the total immediately when the gift-wrap checkbox changes.

issues.title: Important pay action is below the fold
issues.evidence: [11] button "Pay now" (offscreen)
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I had to scroll to see that there is an actual pay button, and I need to be careful not to accidentally purchase anything.
issues.fix: Keep the total and the pay button visible together, or use a sticky checkout summary.

positives: The checkout clearly itemises the book, gift wrap, shipping, and total.
The order name and price are visible immediately.
The empty payment fields give me a clear place to stop without entering any financial information.
review.abandon_reason: I would not continue to payment because the pre-selected £7.99 gift wrap makes the checkout feel misleading, and the task only requires finding the price.

output_reactions.reaction: The cover is simple but does not look like the Watercolour style I selected, and the large misspelling “Adventrue” immediately makes it feel unfinished. I need to inspect the remaining eight pages to see whether the actual family memory came through.

The story is disappointing despite including Sam and the memory elements. “Adventrue” is misspelled, the look does not match my Watercolour choice, and the final sentence shifts oddly to the sky instead of ending with the sandcastles and Grandpa Joe.

console_errors: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)
